summary: Formalizes Dishonor/Rehonor (issue #186): a named Dishonor(card)/Rehonor(card) pair, retrofitted onto every direct .Dishonorable=true assignment. CardPersonalHonor's 'fixed at 0 while Dishonorable' gets an override hook (Utaku Chikako's own passive: a dishonorable Battle Maiden the same owner controls keeps its printed/base value, checked generically against any in-play Personality carrying a matching Effect). New GainHonorFromPerformer negates a Honor gain and rehonors the performer instead if they're dishonorable -- retrofitted onto Doji Shunya's own ability and Shamate Keep's chosen performer. Battle resolution: a dishonorable personality in the army that wins or ties negates the FULL Honor gain from that victory and is rehonored -- for a tie, before DestroyUnits runs, so no double dishonorable-death penalty. Confirmed Justice of the Crane's PrintedKeyword check was already correct (ignores GrantedKeywords, so its own AttachGrantsKeyword grant of Magistrate never satisfies the printed-keyword check) -- just routed through the new Dishonor() helper. Wired Utaku Chikako (Personality Wave 7): the Personal-Honor override passive, plus her Limited ability (gain 2 Honor; a new player-scoped, per-turn MayNotAttackThisTurn flag blocking any non-empty DeclareAttack assignment, resetting at StartTurn). Documented (not coded -- no current consumer) the Recon keyword classification rule in ROADMAP.md, matching Fudo/Fallen's own precedent.
validation: dotnet build clean; full test suite 112/112 core + 34/34 published + 8/8 deck-format; bash tools/check.sh --skip-client all green (13/13 AI, 5/5 server integration, 4/4 client transport integration).
remaining: Kamalakar's Harem (oracle-l5r-10683) needs a DIFFERENT, per-card permanent 'this Personality may not attack' attachment flag -- Utaku Chikako's own restriction is player-and-turn-scoped, not directly reusable there; BLOCKERS note updated to be precise about this. Recon's Timing-prefix half ('Recon Battle'/'Recon Reaction') is documented but not coded -- no card yet to ground which Timing values the prefix actually composes with. No Time For Games (an explicit 'rehonor him' card) is not itself wired, only cited as the illustrative example for the general GainHonorFromPerformer rule.
